name: Monerium EUR emoney
oneLiner: EURE is Monerium's MiCA-regulated euro e-money, minted on SEPA deposits and redeemed 1:1 by an EMI; reserves sit in EUR bank deposits and an LVNAV fund.
collateral: Euro deposits held in segregated accounts with credit institutions and high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) denominated in EUR, separated from Monerium's own funds; over 100% backing maintained as required under MiCA
pegMechanism: Mint-and-burn: EURe is minted when users deposit EUR via SEPA bank transfer after KYC/AML verification, and burned upon redemption back to EUR; peg maintained by licensed EMI with 1:1 backing

jurisdiction.regulator: Financial Supervisory Authority of the Central Bank of Iceland

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25294789: EURE Ethereum owner() = 3/6 Safe 0x5591A6495d726C7EFafb9a9DAD32695D137b4d9f (threshold 3, 6 owners, no modules, no guard). EIP-1967 proxy admin slot = zero. Every addressable mint-capable on-chain surface is confirmed. Issuer-backend model corroborated by Monerium docs and the Safe being the sole control point. Monerium reports annual audits and semi-annual statements, but the latest published table ends at 2024 and aggregates all Monerium e-money rather than independently reconciling EURe token supply; the same page says regular public safeguarded-fund attestations are still being prepared. No qualifying attestor, cadence, or latest EURe report date was found, so reconciliation is unknown. The Central Bank of Iceland authorization matches Monerium EMI ehf. and the issuer page expressly identifies prudential EMI supervision, supporting prudential supervision despite the reconciliation gap.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Monerium documents EURe e-money tokens as live on multiple chains and its SDK describes euro payments minting tokens to wallets and burning tokens for bank payouts. The route is reviewed as issuer-native issuance/redemption, not a third-party bridge.
